entries.title: Cooking Workshop
entries.text: The Food4Thought club invites you to an exciting cooking workshop hosted by the ‘Iolani Gastro students today, Mon, Nov 16, SCIL4F kitchen space during lunch. Enjoy a live cooking demonstration and taste some delicious dishes that transform common holiday leftover items into new culinary sensations while reducing food waste. Space is limited to 30 so make sure to sign up HERE and reserve your spot ASAP! For more info feel free to email achristie@iolani.org.

entries.title: Here's the Tea on Mental Health
entries.text: Curious about what a Health & Wellness Educator does? Want to learn more about social and emotional learning (SEL)? Join us for a casual chat with Ms. Takagi in the Wong- Trainor Lobby (dorm lobby) during lunch, today, Monday, 11/16! Get to know Ms. Takagi, hear more about her role and what she covers in Lifetime Health, and bring your questions about SEL, health, and wellness. Sweet treats provided while supplies last! It's open to all US students! Thank you!

VIRTUAL POP-UP SALE! The Young Entrepreneurs Club invites you to shop at their Virtual Pop-up sale. Pre-orders can be placed, and pickup will be Monday, November 30. Check it out! GRS 9-12: (W.THE CORRECT LINK FROM FRIDAY] FOOD4THOUGHT: CO-OPS! Despite the many obstacles that can make it hard for healthy food to reach our plates, there are strategies that support production, processing, and distribution to consumers! Please watch this 3-minute video and learn how valuable co-ops can be! How can you support co-ops like this one?

entries.title: Letter-writing Project for Foodbank
entries.text: We’re kicking off our annual letter-writing project for the Hawaiʻi Foodbank, aiming for 2500 letters! Students, stop by the tables in the back of the chapel OR in the library to write a quick, happy note; these will be included with the food that keiki take home from school, to their families in need. You can also email Ms. Sakuda in the C+CE Office for a stack of templates for your club or team. Thanks to My Life, My Island, My World for creating these awesome recipes that utilize the Foodbank’s ingredients! GRS 7/8: CHAPEL: LETTER-WRITING PROJECT FOR FOODBANK: We’re kicking off our annual letter-writing project for the Hawaiʻi Foodbank, aiming for 2500 letters! Students, stop by the tables right here, in the back of the chapel to write a quick, happy note; these will be included with the food that keiki take home from school, to their families in need. Thanks to My Life, My Island, My World for creating these awesome recipes that utilize the Foodbank’s ingredients!
